_note:
Slots for [brg_home-community]. Declared beside the fragment so a slot and its {token} ship in one commit. Generated into website/acf/ by `python3 kit/build-acf.py`; never hand-edit an acf.json. Slot names are underscore-only. Defaults are esc_html'd on fill, so write literal characters — a literal `&` and a literal `—`, never `&` or `—`. THE

IS NOT WIRED, and this one is structural rather than awaiting anybody: it carries BOTH a hard
AND an inline marker block. No slot type can hold either — text/textarea escape them into visible markup, and html is an ACF wysiwyg that returns

-wrapped content. The field cannot express the design. Same call as careers-apply's heading. The two image plates and their counter-signed parallax are motion/photography and stay as code; the stand-in photography is tracked as `real-photography`. THE FIRST PARAGRAPH IS intro_1/intro_emphasis/intro_2, NOT body_0 — and the odd numbering is deliberate. It was missed in the first pass (2026-08-13) because the survey regex used to find text was `]*>[^<]*

`, which cannot match a paragraph containing inline tags — so the one wrapping was invisible to the tool and therefore to me. @expo caught it. Rather than renumber body_1/body_2, whose ACF fields are already generated and live, the new paragraph gets its own name: renaming a live field orphans whatever an editor has already typed into it. Cosmetically inconsistent, safe. Leaving it unslotted would have been the worse kind of half-editable: an editor rewrites the founding story in the two paragraphs below while THIS one — which carries the founding claim and the 2013 date — silently contradicts them.

heading_1.label: Heading
heading_1.doc: The section heading. PRESS RETURN to break the line exactly where you want it. The highlighted words are a separate box below, so that the mark can follow them.

heading_2.label: Heading — before the marked words
heading_2.doc: The words on the second line that come immediately before the highlighted ones.

heading_mark.label: Heading — the marked words
heading_mark.doc: The words the highlight sits behind. Keep it short: the mark is drawn to the width of these words, and a long phrase stretches it thin.

intro_1.label: Intro — before the emphasis
intro_1.doc: Opening clause, up to the colon. The space before the bold phrase is in the markup, so no trailing space here.
intro_1.default: Blacktop Restaurant Group started with a simple belief:

intro_emphasis.label: Intro — bold phrase
intro_emphasis.doc: Rendered bold, mid-sentence. A clause, not a paragraph.
intro_emphasis.default: that a great meal is really just an excuse to connect.

intro_2.label: Intro — after the emphasis
intro_2.doc: The rest of the paragraph. Carries the founding year, so it needs editing if that is ever restated.
intro_2.default: Since 2013, we've been growing a family of restaurant brands rooted in genuine hospitality, craft food, and a deep love for the communities we call home.

body_1.label: Body copy — first paragraph
body_1.doc: Plain text; markup is escaped. Write `—` as a literal em dash.
body_1.default: We're not a corporation chasing locations — we're operators who eat at our own restaurants, know our guests by name, and measure success by how many times someone walks out the door smiling.

body_2.label: Body copy — second paragraph
body_2.doc: Carries the live location counts, so it needs editing whenever they change — which is the main reason it is a field. Write `&` and `—` as literal characters. CROSS-SECTION FACT — this number also appears in `our-restaurants-brands` -> Board & Brew second paragraph, and `community-stats` -> Stat 1 figure. Going ACF-editable REMOVED the check that used to catch a mismatch: it was three greppable strings in the repo, and it is now three database rows that nothing repo-side can compare. If you change one, change all three. (`doc` strings are per-field by construction, so this warning has to be repeated in each — there is nowhere on this project that can hold a cross-section fact.)
body_2.default: Today, BRG operates 12 Board & Brew locations across San Diego and Orange County, plus Odie's Pizza Co. in Oceanside — and we're just getting started.

hl_variant.label: Highlight animation
hl_variant.doc: How the marker highlight behind “for community.” arrives. `h3` (default) rough hand-drawn block + ~5deg angled wipe, closest to the comps. `h1` background wipe — THE ONLY ONE THAT SURVIVES A LINE WRAP. `h0` static, no animation, which is what this mark did before. Unknown or blank renders a static painted mark, never blank. Color and padding are unchanged from the original design. Catalog: website/lab/README.md.

photo_1.label: Photo — tall, front
photo_1.doc: The taller photo in front. Portrait crop, around 733x1100. Leave empty to keep the current picture.

photo_1_tone.label: Photo — tall, front — color
photo_1_tone.doc: Color is the default. Switch this photo to black and white when you want it that way on purpose — the photography on this site was only ever gray because the placeholder images were. Affects this photo alone.

photo_1_px.label: Photo — tall, front — movement
photo_1_px.doc: How far this photo drifts inside its frame as you scroll, as a percentage of the frame's height. 0 is off. The dropdown this replaces offered 6, 10 and 16 as Subtle, Medium and Strong, so anything already set still reads exactly the same — you can now pick the values in between. 40 is the ceiling: the page itself stops there, so a larger number would do nothing. The photo is laid out taller than its frame and slides within it, so an edge never appears and it is never zoomed.

photo_1_px_dir.label: Photo — tall, front — movement direction
photo_1_px_dir.doc: Which way this photo travels as the page scrolls. Neighboring photos set in opposite directions are what reads as depth.

photo_1_float.label: Photo — tall, front — frame drift
photo_1_float.doc: Moves the whole frame across the section, on top of the movement inside it, as a percentage of the frame's height. 0 is off; 8 and 12 were the old Gentle and Strong. 40 is the ceiling. Leave this off for a photo that fills its section edge to edge — there is nothing behind it to reveal.

photo_1_float_dir.label: Photo — tall, front — drift direction
photo_1_float_dir.doc: Which way this frame drifts. Set a large and a small photo in opposite directions.

photo_2.label: Photo — behind
photo_2.doc: The photo set behind and slightly offset. Portrait crop, around 548x820. Leave empty to keep the current picture.

photo_2_tone.label: Photo — behind — color
photo_2_tone.doc: Color is the default. Switch this photo to black and white when you want it that way on purpose — the photography on this site was only ever gray because the placeholder images were. Affects this photo alone.

photo_2_px.doc: How far this photo drifts inside its frame as you scroll, as a percentage of the frame's height. 0 is off. The dropdown this replaces offered 6, 10 and 16 as Subtle, Medium and Strong, so anything already set still reads exactly the same — you can now pick the values in between. 40 is the ceiling: the page itself stops there, so a larger number would do nothing. The photo is laid out taller than its frame and slides within it, so an edge never appears and it is never zoomed.

photo_2_px_dir.label: Photo — behind — movement direction
photo_2_px_dir.doc: Which way this photo travels as the page scrolls. Neighboring photos set in opposite directions are what reads as depth.

Leave this off for a photo that fills its section edge to edge — there is nothing behind it to reveal.

photo_2_float_dir.doc: Which way this frame drifts. Set a large and a small photo in opposite directions.

section_bg.label: Section background
section_bg.doc: A pattern or photo filling this whole section, behind everything else. Leave it empty — as it is now — and the section keeps the plain color it has today; nothing changes until you choose something. It is cropped to fill, so the exact size does not matter. ON A DARK SECTION USE A LIGHT OR GRAY ARTWORK: a black pattern over a black panel stays invisible however high you set the strength below.

section_bg_mobile.label: Section background — phones
section_bg_mobile.doc: Optional. A version of the background for phones, used below 768px wide. Leave it empty and the main background above is used at every size. Worth setting when the main artwork is wide: cropped to a narrow screen it often shows nothing recognizable, and a tall or simplified version reads far better.

section_bg_opacity.label: Background strength
section_bg_opacity.doc: How strongly the background shows through. Choose 100% when the artwork already has the intended strength built into the file — anything lower then fades a graphic that was supplied ready to use. Use the lower values when a full-strength image would compete with the words in front of it.

section_bg_px.label: Background movement
section_bg_px.doc: Drifts the background as the page scrolls, behind the content, as a percentage of the section's height. 0 is off — the right starting point, because a pattern moving too fast pulls the eye away from the copy. 6 is subtle, 10 medium, 16 strong, and anything in between is allowed. 40 is the ceiling; the page stops there.

section_bg_px_dir.label: Background movement direction
section_bg_px_dir.doc: Which way the background travels as the page scrolls. Only matters once movement above is above 0. Neighboring sections set in opposite directions are what reads as depth rather than as one sheet sliding.

mark_1_bolt_art.label: Artwork
mark_1_bolt_art.doc: Which mark is drawn here. Leave it alone to keep the one the design uses. Any SVG or PNG from the media library works; SVG stays crisp at any size.

mark_1_bolt_pos.label: Position
mark_1_bolt_pos.doc: Where the mark sits in its section. "Where the design put it" is the starting point and leaves it exactly where it is now — choose one of the nine only when you want to move it. Corners sit inside the section padding, so a long headline cannot push a mark down into the type.

mark_1_bolt_opacity.label: Opacity
mark_1_bolt_opacity.doc: How solid the mark is. 100 is as drawn; lower settles it into the background.

mark_1_bolt_show.label: Show this mark
mark_1_bolt_show.doc: Hiding removes just this one mark. Nothing else in the section changes.

mark_1_bolt_anim.label: Animation
mark_1_bolt_anim.doc: How the mark moves. "As built" keeps what it does today — a hard-cut jitter for most, a spin for the asterisk in the hero cluster. Still stops it entirely. Anyone who has switched off animation in their system settings sees it still whatever is chosen here.

mark_2_all_trim_art.label: Artwork
mark_2_all_trim_art.doc: Which mark is drawn here. Leave it alone to keep the one the design uses. Any SVG or PNG from the media library works; SVG stays crisp at any size.

mark_2_all_trim_pos.label: Position
mark_2_all_trim_pos.doc: Where the mark sits in its section. "Where the design put it" is the starting point and leaves it exactly where it is now — choose one of the nine only when you want to move it. Corners sit inside the section padding, so a long headline cannot push a mark down into the type.

mark_2_all_trim_opacity.label: Opacity
mark_2_all_trim_opacity.doc: How solid the mark is. 100 is as drawn; lower settles it into the background.

mark_2_all_trim_show.label: Show this mark
mark_2_all_trim_show.doc: Hiding removes just this one mark. Nothing else in the section changes.

mark_2_all_trim_anim.doc: How the mark moves. "As built" keeps what it does today — a hard-cut jitter for most, a spin for the asterisk in the hero cluster. Still stops it entirely. Anyone who has switched off animation in their system settings sees it still whatever is chosen here.

cta_position.label: Where the buttons sit
cta_position.doc: At the bottom is the usual place and the one the rest of the site uses.

choices.foot: At the bottom of the section
choices.head: Directly under the heading

btn_color.label: Button color
btn_color.doc: The button's color. "As designed" is the starting point and leaves this section's buttons exactly as they look today — which matters, because several sections paint theirs black on purpose and the give-back slider alternates yellow and black down the slides. Choose a color and it takes over. The words flip to black or white automatically, whichever reads on the color you pick. This applies to every button in this section.

btn_style.label: Filled or outline
btn_style.doc: Filled is a solid block of color. Outline draws the color as a ring with the words in it and nothing behind — useful over a photo, where a solid block can sit heavily. "As designed" leaves it as it is today, which is filled everywhere. Both are exactly the same size, so switching one does not move anything around it.

btn_effect.label: Hover effect
btn_effect.doc:
What the button does when someone points at it. Lift is what every button has always done and stays the default — it rises slightly and casts a shadow. Lift and swap color does that AND flips to the opposite ink, which is the loudest of the set and best kept for one main action on a page. Underline draws a rule under the words and leaves the button still, which reads as a link — a good fit for the small buttons. Grow swells it in place. Press down pushes it into the page. Fill in floods an outline button with its color, so pair it with Outline. None holds it still.

This is the HOVER only; the way the button arrives on screen is the site-wide reveal. Anyone who has switched off animation sees no hover movement whatever is chosen.

buttons.label: Buttons
buttons.doc:
Buttons for this section. Add as many as you need — they sit in a row and wrap onto the next line on a narrow screen. Leave the list empty, as it is now, and the section has no buttons at all and looks exactly as it does today.

Their color, fill and hover come from Button style below and apply to all of them.

label.label: Label
label.doc: The words on the button. Short reads best: it is set in capitals with wide letter spacing. A button with no label is not drawn.

href.label: Link
href.doc: Where it goes. A path like /careers/ stays on this site, a full address goes off it, and mailto:someone@blacktoprg.com opens a mail window.

popup.label: Open in a pop-up
popup.doc: For a Google Form, choose Pop-up and it opens in a panel over the page instead of sending people to Google. A form that is set to require a Google sign-in CANNOT be shown this way — Google's sign-in page refuses to be embedded and the panel comes up blank — so that one has to stay on Open the link until its Responses settings are changed. Anything that is not a form stays on Open the link.

modal_bg.label: Pop-up background
modal_bg.doc: The color of the panel a form opens in. Match it to the form's own Theme color in Google Forms and the two read as one surface. This cannot color the form itself — that is Google's page on Google's domain.
